scenes.tts: How can a population change when no individual changes its inherited trait? Watch this schematic herd. Each animal keeps its color through life, but the colored shares can change when a new generation replaces the old.
scenes.caption: How can a population change when no individual changes its inherited trait? Watch this schematic herd. Each animal keeps its color through life, but the colored shares can change when a new generation replaces the old.
scenes.visual: Hook on a dark ground. A large schematic herd fills the frame: simple elephant silhouettes, teal for a tuskless inherited variant and gold for a tusked inherited variant. A thin label reads 'schematic'. Individuals drift slowly but never change color. The whole herd slides toward a faint next-generation outline.
scenes.narration: How can a population change when no individual changes its inherited trait? Watch this schematic herd. Each animal keeps its color through life, but the colored shares can change when a new generation replaces the old.

scenes.visual: Brief title card, How Populations Change. Keep two large moving markers behind the title: teal means tuskless inherited variant; gold means tusked inherited variant.

scenes.tts: Individuals in one population are not identical. Some differences come from food or experience. Others are inherited. Only inherited differences can pass from parents to offspring, so those differences can shape later generations.
scenes.caption: Individuals in one population are not identical. Some differences come from food or experience. Others are inherited. Only inherited differences can pass from parents to offspring, so those differences can shape later generations.
scenes.visual: Return to the same full-frame schematic herd. A temporary grey glow marks food or experience, then fades with the individual. Teal and gold color badges move from parent silhouettes to offspring silhouettes. Keep at most four labels.
scenes.narration: Individuals in one population are not identical. Some differences come from food or experience. Others are inherited. Only inherited differences can pass from parents to offspring, so those differences can shape later generations.

scenes.tts: Zoom into the population's gene pool: all its alleles, meaning versions of genes. A mutation can make a new allele. Gene flow can bring an allele from another population. Both can change what the pool contains.
scenes.caption: Zoom into the population's gene pool: all its alleles, meaning versions of genes. A mutation can make a new allele. Gene flow can bring an allele from another population. Both can change what the pool contains.
scenes.visual: Transform the herd into one large labelled bead pool, still marked 'schematic'. Teal and gold beads circulate. Mutation adds one new blue bead from inside the pool. Gene flow moves one blue bead in from a smaller neighboring pool. No molecular structures.
scenes.narration: Zoom into the population's gene pool: all its alleles, meaning versions of genes. A mutation can make a new allele. Gene flow can bring an allele from another population. Both can change what the pool contains.

scenes.tts: Sexual reproduction does something different. Meiosis and fertilization reshuffle alleles that already exist into new combinations. The offspring can differ from both parents without a new allele appearing.
scenes.caption: Sexual reproduction does something different. Meiosis and fertilization reshuffle alleles that already exist into new combinations. The offspring can differ from both parents without a new allele appearing.
scenes.visual: Carry the same bead pool. Existing colored beads pair, separate, and recombine into several offspring pairs. A counter labelled 'new alleles' stays unchanged while 'new combinations' grows. Labels remain large and high contrast.
scenes.narration: Sexual reproduction does something different. Meiosis and fertilization reshuffle alleles that already exist into new combinations. The offspring can differ from both parents without a new allele appearing.

scenes.tts: Now suppose teal and gold individuals leave offspring equally often. Predict the next generation. Will one color steadily take over, or will their shares simply wobble?
scenes.caption: Now suppose teal and gold individuals leave offspring equally often. Predict the next generation. Will one color steadily take over, or will their shares simply wobble?
scenes.visual: Transform beads back into the same schematic herd. Teal and gold individuals enter a wide survival-and-reproduction filter in equal streams. Put the question across the top and keep both streams moving slowly.
scenes.narration: Now suppose teal and gold individuals leave offspring equally often. Predict the next generation. Will one color steadily take over, or will their shares simply wobble?

scenes.visual: Hold the predict question. Teal and gold markers continue drifting at equal rates through the filter. A small question mark pulses; nothing reveals the answer.

scenes.tts: With equal reproductive success, neither color has a consistent advantage. Chance can still make the shares wobble. Yet the model has no directional push toward teal or gold.
scenes.caption: With equal reproductive success, neither color has a consistent advantage. Chance can still make the shares wobble. Yet the model has no directional push toward teal or gold.
scenes.visual: Grow several next-generation rows from equal streams. Their teal shares shift slightly both directions. A large centered arrow stays level and is labelled 'no consistent direction'. Keep 'schematic' visible.
scenes.narration: With equal reproductive success, neither color has a consistent advantage. Chance can still make the shares wobble. Yet the model has no directional push toward teal or gold.

scenes.tts: Real populations usually produce more young than their environments can support. Food, space, predators, disease, and other limits mean many never reproduce. The surviving adults are only part of the story; reproduction matters too.
scenes.caption: Real populations usually produce more young than their environments can support. Food, space, predators, disease, and other limits mean many never reproduce. The surviving adults are only part of the story; reproduction matters too.
scenes.visual: The parent herd produces a broad wave of small offspring markers that fills most of the frame. A narrowing environment gate labelled food, space, predators, and disease lets only some pass. Survivors then move toward offspring nests.
scenes.narration: Real populations usually produce more young than their environments can support. Food, space, predators, disease, and other limits mean many never reproduce. The surviving adults are only part of the story; reproduction matters too.

scenes.tts: Now change the conditions. Suppose teal individuals leave more offspring because their inherited variation fits those conditions better. More teal markers pass through the survival-and-reproduction filter. The next generation starts with a larger teal share.
scenes.caption: Now change the conditions. Suppose teal individuals leave more offspring because their inherited variation fits those conditions better. More teal markers pass through the survival-and-reproduction filter. The next generation starts with a larger teal share.
scenes.visual: Reuse the same filter, now under a large 'changed conditions' banner. Teal markers pass and form offspring more often than gold markers. Build the next generation from those offspring; its teal region grows without any marker changing color.
scenes.narration: Now change the conditions. Suppose teal individuals leave more offspring because their inherited variation fits those conditions better. More teal markers pass through the survival-and-reproduction filter. The next generation starts with a larger teal share.

scenes.tts: When inherited variations affect reproductive success, populations change across generations. That process is natural selection. It needs inherited variation and unequal reproductive success under the current conditions.
scenes.caption: When inherited variations affect reproductive success, populations change across generations. That process is natural selection. It needs inherited variation and unequal reproductive success under the current conditions.
scenes.visual: Compress the carried world into a three-part flow across the full frame: inherited variation, unequal offspring left, changed next generation. Teal and gold markers travel continuously through all three parts. Reveal 'natural selection' only after the transformation completes.
scenes.narration: When inherited variations affect reproductive success, populations change across generations. That process is natural selection. It needs inherited variation and unequal reproductive success under the current conditions.

scenes.tts: Follow one gold individual. It never turns teal. Follow one teal individual. It never turns gold. The changing pattern appears only when we compare the population across generations.
scenes.caption: Follow one gold individual. It never turns teal. Follow one teal individual. It never turns gold. The changing pattern appears only when we compare the population across generations.
scenes.visual: Track one large gold silhouette and one large teal silhouette through their lives with bright outlines. Neither color changes. Pull back to compare old and new population rows, where only the shares differ.
scenes.narration: Follow one gold individual. It never turns teal. Follow one teal individual. It never turns gold. The changing pattern appears only when we compare the population across generations.

scenes.tts: Selection can work only with variation that is present. If every marker begins gold and no new teal allele appears or arrives, a teal advantage cannot change the population. Conditions cannot select a variant that is absent.
scenes.caption: Selection can work only with variation that is present. If every marker begins gold and no new teal allele appears or arrives, a teal advantage cannot change the population. Conditions cannot select a variant that is absent.
scenes.visual: Reset the schematic field to all gold markers. A teal-shaped opening in the filter glows, but no teal marker exists to enter it. Mutation and gene-flow entrances stay visibly closed. Keep the result labelled 'variant absent'.
scenes.narration: Selection can work only with variation that is present. If every marker begins gold and no new teal allele appears or arrives, a teal advantage cannot change the population. Conditions cannot select a variant that is absent.

scenes.tts: Whether a variation helps, harms, or has no effect often depends on the environment. Selection does not plan ahead, and organisms do not change inherited traits because they need them.
scenes.caption: Whether a variation helps, harms, or has no effect often depends on the environment. Selection does not plan ahead, and organisms do not change inherited traits because they need them.
scenes.visual: Slide the conditions banner between two schematic environments. The same teal and gold markers receive different filter widths in each setting. A forward-pointing planning arrow appears, then fades under the label 'no planning'.
scenes.narration: Whether a variation helps, harms, or has no effect often depends on the environment. Selection does not plan ahead, and organisms do not change inherited traits because they need them.

scenes.tts: Return to the whole field. Different individuals entered, some left more offspring, and the next generation has a different mix. The population changed because reproductive success differed, not because individuals transformed.
scenes.caption: Return to the whole field. Different individuals entered, some left more offspring, and the next generation has a different mix. The population changed because reproductive success differed, not because individuals transformed.
scenes.visual: Fill the frame with the starting and next-generation schematic herds. Curved paths connect unchanged teal and gold parents to offspring. The next generation settles with a changed mix while both individual colors remain fixed.
scenes.narration: Return to the whole field. Different individuals entered, some left more offspring, and the next generation has a different mix. The population changed because reproductive success differed, not because individuals transformed.

scenes.visual: End card with one line only: 'When inherited variations affect reproductive success, populations change across generations.'
